text: Under the Designs Act 2000, a 'design' means only the features of shape, configuration, pattern, ornament or composition of lines or colours applied to any article by any industrial process or means, which appeal to and are judged solely by the eye. Designs protect the visual appearance, NOT function. For AYUSH products, registrable designs include: unique bottle shapes for Ayurvedic oils, distinctive packaging configurations, ornamental patterns on medicine boxes, label designs and artwork, unique tablet/capsule shapes (if novel). NOT registrable: functional features (those are patents), trademarks/logos (separate registration), designs dictated by function, immoral designs.

Design registration in India: 1) Prior art search — check Design Search Database on ipindia.gov.in for similar designs. 2) Prepare representation sheets — 4 identical sets of drawings/photographs from different views (front, back, top, side, perspective). 3) File application (Form 1) with the Patent Office (also handles designs) — can designate Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, or Kolkata. 4) Examination for novelty and distinctiveness — typically 3-6 months. 5) If objections raised, respond within prescribed time. 6) Registration certificate issued upon acceptance. 7) Design published in the Official Design Journal. Timeline: 6-9 months for straightforward applications. E-filing available on ipindia.gov.in.

Design registration fees in India (2024): Filing fee for natural persons/startups/small entities: Rs 1,000 (e-filing) or Rs 1,100 (physical). Filing fee for others (companies): Rs 4,000 (e-filing) or Rs 4,400 (physical). Per-design fee — if filing multiple related designs, each costs separately. Restoration fee (if not renewed): Rs 2,000 (natural persons) or Rs 8,000 (others). Renewal fee: Rs 2,000 (natural persons) or Rs 4,000 (others) for extending from 10 to 15 years. Request for examination fee: included in filing. Certified copy fee: Rs 500.

IP protection comparison for AYUSH innovations: DESIGN (Designs Act 2000) — protects visual appearance/shape, 15-year term, requires novelty in appearance, no functionality protection, quick registration. PATENT (Patents Act 1970) — protects technical invention/method, 20-year term, requires novelty + inventive step + industrial applicability, covers function, slower process. TRADEMARK (Trade Marks Act 1999) — protects brand identifiers, indefinite term (renewable), requires distinctiveness, no appearance/function protection. Example: A novel Ayurvedic medicine in a unique bottle — Patent the formulation, Design register the bottle shape, Trademark the brand name.

A design must be new and original to be registrable. 'New' means not disclosed to the public anywhere in the world before the filing date (absolute novelty). 'Original' means it originated from the applicant, not copied. Disclosure destroying novelty includes: prior publication, prior sale, prior public display, online posting. Grace period: If design was disclosed at an official or recognized exhibition in India, can still file within 6 months of exhibition opening. For AYUSH packaging: avoid showing new designs at trade fairs before filing; file first, then exhibit. Combination of known elements can be novel if the overall visual impression is new.

Designs are classified under the Locarno Classification (32 classes). Relevant classes for AYUSH: Class 9 (packages and containers) — bottles, jars, boxes for medicines/cosmetics, Class 19 (stationery, office equipment) — if marketing materials have unique design, Class 24 (medical apparatus) — medical devices with unique design, Class 28 (pharmaceutical and cosmetic products) — tablet shapes, cream containers, dropper designs. Filing in correct class is mandatory. Multi-class filing allowed but fees multiply. Check Locarno Classification on WIPO website to identify correct class for your AYUSH product design.

Initial design registration term: 10 years from filing date. Renewal: Can extend for 5 more years (total 15 years) by paying renewal fee before expiry of initial 10 years. After 15 years, design enters public domain — anyone can use it. No further extension possible (unlike trademarks which are indefinite). For AYUSH businesses: if packaging design becomes iconic, consider trademarking the shape as trade dress (3D trademark) for perpetual protection. Keep design registration for the 15-year exclusive period, then rely on trademark trade dress if applicable.

Design piracy occurs when someone manufactures/sells articles bearing a registered design without authorization. Section 22 of Designs Act 2000 provides remedies: contract price for pirated article or Rs 50,000 (whichever is greater) for each article pirated (civil remedy). Also can seek injunction and damages. For AYUSH packaging: if competitors copy your registered bottle shape or packaging design, send cease-and-desist letter referencing registration number, then file suit in District Court. Criminal remedies not available for design piracy (unlike trademark counterfeiting). Maintain evidence: purchase samples of infringing products, take photographs, retain receipts.

To protect designs internationally: 1) Hague Agreement (India NOT yet a member as of 2024) — single international application covering 90+ countries (not available for Indian applicants directly). 2) Paris Convention priority — file in other countries within 6 months of Indian filing to claim priority date. 3) Direct national filing — file separately in each country. For AYUSH exporters to USA, EU, UK: must file separately in each jurisdiction. US design patent term: 15 years. EU Registered Community Design: 25 years (5+5+5+5+5). UK Registered Design: 25 years. Coordinate with local IP attorneys in each target country.

India does NOT recognize unregistered design rights — registration is mandatory for protection. This differs from UK/EU which have unregistered design rights (3 years automatic protection). Consequence: in India, if you don't register your design, anyone can copy it without legal consequence. Copyright may cover artistic works but not industrial designs applied to functional articles in quantity (more than 50 items — Section 15(2) of Copyright Act). Lesson for AYUSH businesses: register designs BEFORE commercial launch. Once you sell products, novelty may be lost for registration purposes.
